extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and authors typesetting mathematics with TeX (TeX users)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and concrete rules for high-quality mathematical typesetting with plain TeX: spacing, delimiters, ellipses, line breaking, braces, matrices, vertical spacing, and other fine typographic details. Intended to help authors produce visually correct and readable mathematical formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: mu units: use \mskip/\mkern only with mu
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX insists that \mskip and \mkern be used only with mu; conversely, \hskip and \kern (also allowed in formulas) must never give units in mu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: \mskip (muglue) inserts glue in mu units; use :\mkern: when there is no stretch/shrink. Do not mix mu units with \hskip/\kern.

rubrics_metrics.name: thin space before differentials (\,)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulas involving calculus look best when an extra thin space appears before d (e.g., dx, du).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert \, before differentials: \int_{-\infty}^0 f(x)\,dx, y\,dx-x\,dy, dx\,dy = r\,dr\,d\theta. Exception: no \, needed when dt appears by itself in the numerator of a fraction (visual detachment). Use judgement whether a \,' is desirable in a given example.

rubrics_metrics.name: physical units in roman with thin space
rubrics_metrics.description: When physical units appear in a formula, they should be set in roman type and separated from the preceding material by a thin space.

rubrics_metrics.name: thin space after factorial (!) before letters/numbers/delimiters
rubrics_metrics.description: Thin spaces should be inserted after exclamation points (which stand for the factorial operation in a formula) if the next character is a letter or a number or an opening delimiter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: $(2n)!/\bigl(n!\,(n+1)!\bigr)$ should be typeset with a thin space after ! to avoid crowding. Also applied in multinomial/factorial expressions like ${52!\over13!\,13!\,26!}$.

rubrics_metrics.name: use \,, \! to fix optical spacing glitches
rubrics_metrics.description: When symbols are bunched too tightly or too loosely, add \,, \! (thin or negative thin space) to improve visual appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common candidates: \sqrt2\,x, \sqrt{\,\log x}, 0\bigl(i/\sqrt n\,\bigr), [\,0,1), x'2\!/2, n/\!\log n, \Gamma_{\!2}+\Delta'\{\!2\}, R_i{}'j{}_{\!kl}, \int\!\!\!\int_D dx\,dy. Use first proofs to spot and correct such optical problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX math atom types and inter-atomic spacing table
rubrics_metrics.description: A formula is converted to a math list of atoms of eight basic types (Ord, Op, Bin, Rel, Open, Close, Punct, Inner). A spacing table determines what space (none, thin, medium, thick) to insert between adjacent atom pairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table entries 0,1,2,3 correspond to no space, thin, medium, thick; parenthesized entries are inserted only in display/text styles, not in script/scriptscript styles. Fractions are treated as Inner; other constructs may be treated as Ord. Appendix G has precise conversion details. Subscripts/superscripts attach to atoms without changing atomic type.

rubrics_metrics.name: \left/\right vs \bigl/\bigr/\bigm/\big: different atom types affect spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: The plain TeX macros \bigl, \bigr, \bigm and \big produce identical delimiters but make them different atom types (Open, Close, Rel, Ord respectively); \left...\right encloses the subformula into an Inner atom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because atom types affect spacing, \left...\right (Inner) can produce more space around a subformula than \bigl...\bigr (Open/Close). Use \mathinner{\bigl( (subformula)\bigr)} to force \big-size delimiters but behave like \left..\right except when the subformula ends with Punct.

rubrics_metrics.name: use \left/\right to correct delimiter-like symbols treated as ordinary
rubrics_metrics.description: When symbols like | or || are treated as ordinary symbols (Ord) rather than delimiters, spacing can be wrong; use \left and \right so TeX recognizes them as delimiters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 1- x| = 1+x| has wrong spacing if | is treated as ordinary; \left|...\right| yields correct spacing. Other delimiters (floor/ceiling) are known to TeX and need no correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellipsis: use \ldots vs \cdots appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish low dots (\ldots) and centered dots (\cdots). Use \cdots between + and \times and between = and similar relations; use \ldots between commas or when terms are juxtaposed with no signs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: x_1+\cdots+x_n, x_1=\cdots=x_n=0, A_1\times\cdots\times A_n, f(x_1,\ldots,x_n), x_1x_2\ldots x_n, (1-x)(1-x-2)\ldots(1-x-n). Special case: when ellipses are at the very end of a formula or just before a closing delimiter, add an extra thin space (\,) ; plain TeX allows \dots in text as abbreviation for $\ldots\,$.

rubrics_metrics.name: line breaking in math: where breaks are allowed and how to control them
rubrics_metrics.description: A formula will be broken only after a relation symbol (e.g., =, <, ~) or after a binary operation symbol (+, -, \times, \cdot) when that symbol is at the outer level of the formula; TeX will not break after commas in math mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you don't want breaks at certain places, freeze subformulas with extra braces so they become unbreakable boxes. Use a discretionary multiplication sign \* to permit a break similar to \- (but inserts a \times in text size if it breaks). Use \allowbreak to permit an outer-level break at a given point. Penalties: \relpenalty and \binoppenalty control break penalties (plain TeX defaults: \relpenalty=500, \binoppenalty=700). Use \penalty(number) after an atom to override. \nobreak is an abbreviation for \penalty10000.

rubrics_metrics.name: braces and set-builder spacing: use \{ \} and \mid with thin spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: In set notation use \{ and \} for braces and use \mid for the vertical bar in set-builder expressions; insert thin spaces inside the braces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: \{\,x\mid x>5\,\} or \{\,x:x>5\,\}. Some authors prefer colon instead of \mid. For larger delimiters use \bigl, \bigm, \bigr (or \Big, \bigg, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: cases environment syntax and alignment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \cases to typeset piecewise definitions; each case has two parts separated by & (left part is math, right part is text) and each case line must end with \cr. \cases typesets its own '{' automatically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blank spaces after & are ignored. Use \noalign{...} immediately after any \cr within \cases to insert vertical-mode material (e.g., \noalign{\vskip2pt} to add space between cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: overbrace/underbrace behave like large operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Horizontal braces set over or under parts of a displayed formula use \overbrace or \underbrace, which are treated as large operators and can take limits above or below.

rubrics_metrics.name: matrix constructions: \matrix, \pmatrix, \bordermatrix and alignment tokens
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \matrix for rectangular arrays: entries separated by &, rows ended with \cr. Put your own \left and \right delimiters around \matrix; \pmatrix supplies parentheses. Use \bordermatrix for matrices with row/column labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries are centered; each column is as wide as needed and there is a quad between columns. Use \hfill at the start/end of an entry to flush-right/flush-left. Small inline matrices can be produced with constructions such as {a\atop b} or by grouping. For ellipses in matrices use \vdots and \ddots as companions to \ldots.

rubrics_metrics.name: vertical spacing tools: \phantom, \vphantom, \hphantom, \smash, \mathstrut, \raise/\lower
rubrics_metrics.description: Control vertical/horizontal space of invisible boxes with \phantom (width+height+depth), \vphantom (height+depth but zero width), \hphantom (width but zero height/depth), and \smash (sets height+depth to zero). \mathstrut is a convenient vertical strut; \raise and \lower adjust box positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: \phantom{(subformula)}, \vphantom, \mathop{\smash\limsup\vphantom\liminf} to adjust operator heights. Use \raise with explicit box and style (e.g., \raise\pt\hbox{\scriptscriptstyle n}). For global tuning of subscript/superscript positions, adjust \fontdimen parameters (e.g., \fontdimen16\tensy) but be careful as they are global.

rubrics_metrics.name: special math-mode primitives for format designers (\nonscript, \everymath, \everydisplay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced primitives allow fine control: \nonscript prevents glue/kern from being used in script/scriptscript styles; \everymath and \everydisplay insert token lists before reading inline/display math.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \nonscript\; to produce the exact spacing corresponding to a particular table entry in non-script styles. Use \everymath={...} or \everydisplay={...} to preset conventions/tokens applied to all formulas.
